title: Soup loop iteration record
description: A snapshot of one harvest -> train -> verdict -> canary cycle, appended to .soup-loops/iterations.jsonl (default layout) each time the iteration advances; the latest line per iteration_id wins. Which version is active is NOT read from here but from the version log (version.schema.json). The first deployed model is a seed line: parent_iteration_id and from_version null, to_version 1, outcome promoted. Readers ignore unknown fields.

parent_iteration_id.description: The iteration whose version this one started from; null for the seed line.

from_version.description: The version that was active when the iteration started; null for the seed line.

to_version.description: The version this iteration produces; null when it ended before producing one.

finished_at.description: When the iteration reached a final outcome; null while it is still running or in canary.

until.description: Cursor: conversation and feedback lines with ts up to and including this moment were considered. The next iteration reads only newer lines.

feedback.description: Feedback lines counted after the latest-wins rule.

dataset.description: The training data built from the harvest.

method.description: The Soup training task, e.g. dpo or kto.

base.description: What training actually loaded as its starting point (a base model id, or a merged earlier version's directory).

root_base.description: The original base model id the version line descends from, when base is a merged earlier version.

decision.description: SHIP and DON'T SHIP are soup ship's decisions; SKIPPED and ERROR mean no verdict was reached, and the iteration does not roll out.

baseline.description: What the candidate was compared against.

ref.description: What was loaded as the baseline: a base model id (kind base), or the served name or path of an earlier version (kind version).

version.description: The baseline's version number; required when kind is version.

corrections.description: Optional. Check 1, corrections learned: did the new version learn the answers a person corrected? Absent = not measured. When present, all fields are present.

fixed.description: Edits whose paraphrases the new version hit more often than the old version did.

broken.description: Edits whose paraphrases the new version hit less often than the old version did.

ties.description: Edits where both versions had the same number of hits.

n_edits.description: The edits checked: fixed + broken + ties.

n_paraphrases.description: The paraphrases (paraphrase records, latest per answer) the edits were checked with, summed over the edits.

p_value.description: One-sided sign test over fixed vs broken: the chance of at least this many fixed if fixing and breaking were equally likely. null when fixed + broken is 0.

outcome.description: insufficient: the iteration had edits but fewer than 5 discordant ones (fixed + broken). not_applicable: the training set held no edits, so there were no corrections to check.

held_out.description: Optional. Check 2, non-inferiority on held-out edits: edits kept out of training, scored with the same metric against their corrected text and paired by prompt. The new version must not be significantly below the old one. Absent = not measured. When present, all required fields are present.

better.description: Held-out edits the new version scored higher on than the old one.

worse.description: Held-out edits the new version scored lower on than the old one.

ties.description: Held-out edits both versions scored the same on.

n.description: The held-out edits scored: better + worse + ties.

p_value.description: One-sided sign test over worse vs better: the chance of at least this many worse if the two versions were equally good. null when better + worse is 0.

outcome.description: pass: the new version is not significantly below the old one. fail: it is. weak: fewer than 10 held-out edits, too few to trust a pass. not_measured: fewer than 5 held-out edits.

style.description: Optional. How a pairwise judge preferred the new version's held-out answers to the old version's. Information only: it is recorded but never decides the outcome.

p_value.description: p-value of the split between preferred_new and preferred_old; null when there is nothing to test.

samples.description: Answers observed per bucket during this canary.

verdict.description: UNKNOWN: too few samples so far.

quality.description: Optional. The evidence behind the answer-quality part of the canary verdict: rated answers and negative feedback per bucket, and the significance test over them. Writers that do not judge quality omit it; readers ignore it when absent.

verdict.description: OK: no significant regression (at the minimum this means none was detected, not that the models are equal). MAJOR: the canary's negative share is higher by more than the threshold and the difference is significant. UNKNOWN: fewer than min_rated rated answers in a bucket so far. INSUFFICIENT: the maximum wait ran out below the minimum.

rated.description: Answers that received feedback, per bucket.

negative.description: Rated answers that received negative feedback, per bucket.

share.description: negative / rated per bucket; null while the bucket has no rated answers.

difference.description: Canary share minus stable share; null when either share is null.

z.description: Pooled two-proportion z statistic; positive means the canary is worse. null when it is undefined (a bucket without rated answers, or all rated answers on the same side of negative / not negative).

p_value.description: One-sided p-value of z (the chance of a gap this large or larger if both buckets were equally good); null when z is null.

min_rated.description: Rated answers required in each bucket before a verdict other than UNKNOWN or INSUFFICIENT is given.

threshold.description: The largest tolerated rise in the negative share (0.05 = 5 percentage points).

timed_out.description: True when the maximum wait for ratings ran out before min_rated was reached.

decided_on.description: errors_only: the rollout was decided on the error rates alone, because the quality evidence never reached the minimum in time.

artifacts.description: What is needed to serve this iteration's version again.

served_as.description: The name the version is served under: a soup serve adapter name, or an Ollama tag such as myproj:v2.

outcome.description: running: not past the verdict yet. canary: serving a share of traffic. promoted: to_version became the active version. rolled_back: the canary was withdrawn. skipped: nothing to train or no verdict reached. failed: a stage errored.

reason.description: Why the iteration has this outcome, in plain words.

^x_[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$.description: Producer extension namespace (x_<app>). Soup never reads or rewrites it.

iteration_id.description: Unique, safe as a directory name. soup-cli writes iter-<UTC YYYYMMDDTHHMMSS>-<8 hex>.

utc_timestamp.description: ISO 8601 date-time in UTC, suffix Z or +00:00.

template_ref.description: An instruction template: a stable id and the version of its text.

scoring.description: How an answer was scored against a corrected text.

method.description: added_recall scores what the correction ADDED: the added words are the edit's content words that the original answer lacked, and an answer is a hit when at least threshold of them are present (when an edit adds fewer than 2 content words, all its content words are used instead). reference_judge asks a judge model to compare the answer with the corrected text.

threshold.description: added_recall: the share of the added words an answer must contain to be a hit (0.5). null when the method has no threshold.

template.description: reference_judge: the judge's instruction template. null when the method uses none.
